Command: Dwell in booths for seven days
Summary: For seven days, all Israelites born in Israel dwell in booths, remembering that God made Israel dwell in booths when he brought them out of Egypt.
Commandment: Dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know God made Israel dwell in booths in the wilderness.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The booths turned memory into dwelling: for a week each year Israel lived again as the wilderness generation lived. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
